articles.title: Kyle Monangai Injury, New Rumors on Bears RB's Status & Fantasy Implications for Week 5 vs. Packers
articles.summary: Kyle Monangai is in the middle of a breakout season, but the Chicago Bears running back's status reportedly is up in the air heading into a Week 5 clash against the Green Bay Packers.
articles.body:
Kyle Monangai is in the middle of a breakout season, but the Chicago Bears running back's status reportedly is up in the air heading into a Week 5 clash against the Green Bay Packers.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler, Monangai is dealing with a turf toe injury that he's hoping to play through, but there's a chance he won't be available this week or next.

Monangai, who is in his second NFL season, has had a tremendous start to the 2026 campaign, rushing for 324 yards, the seventh-best mark in the league, along with three touchdowns on 60 carries. His 5.4 yards per carry ranks sixth in the NFL this season.

He's coming off a 146-yard, two-touchdown performance in a 23-12 win against the New York Jets on Sunday.

Monangai potentially missing this week has fantasy implications as well. Given his uncertainty heading into the game, managers will likely need to have a replacement ready just in case he's unable to go.

One option that could still be available is the Chargers' Keaton Mitchell, who has been getting increasingly more touches throughout the season. Philadelphia's Will Shipley also has the chance to get more action this week since Saquon Barkley is week-to-week and Tank Bigsby is set to undergo core muscle surgery .

The Bears will hope to have him on the field this week in a divisional matchup with the Packers, but the good news is they have another strong backfield option with D'Andre Swift.

Swift, who is in his third season in Chicago, has rushed for 311 yards and three touchdowns through four games. Unfortunately for the Bears, Swift is questionable heading into Sunday's game because of hip and knee injuries. He did not practice on Wednesday and was limited on Thursday.

The two backfield injuries come amid a hamstring injury to star quarterback Caleb Williams. The third-year player suffered the injury in Week 2 against the Minnesota Vikings and has missed the last two weeks.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson said earlier this week that Tyson Bagent would once again be the starter for Chicago as Williams works his way back to the field.

Even with Williams missing the past two weeks, the Bears have gotten off to a 3-1 start as they look to get back to the playoffs following a strong 2025 campaign. Chicago will look to pick up a rivalry win on Sunday, but the status of its running backs will be a big factor in whether it can leave Lambeau Field victorious.

articles.title: Jason Kelce donates $8,000 to leukemia-stricken Eagles fan as fundraiser nears $150,000 goal
articles.summary: Earlier this year, a Bucks County Eagles fan facing a devastating health battle received a major show of support from Jason Kelce.
articles.body: Earlier this year, a Bucks County Eagles fan facing a devastating health battle received a major show of support from Jason Kelce. Tom Trampe, known to many fans as “Chomp,” had gone viral years ago for his passion for the Philadelphia Eagles. After being diagnosed with leukemia and undergoing emergency brain surgery, Trampe and his family faced a difficult road ahead. A community fundraiser has since drawn widespread support, including an $8,000 contribution from Kelce.Jason Kelce donates $8,000 to Tom Trampe’s fundraiserTrampe became a familiar face among Eagles fans after a viral video captured his determination to suit up for Philadelphia. Years later, his fight is no longer about stepping onto an NFL field. articles.title: Bengals Safety Reveals Malik Willis Has a Tell on Pass Plays Ahead of Week 5 Game vs. Dolphins
articles.summary: The Cincinnati Bengals apparently have a tell on Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis going into Sunday's game, but it's no longer a secret.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals apparently have a tell on Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis going into Sunday's game, but it's no longer a secret.

That's because safety Jordan Battle revealed it on Thursday.

"He has a little slight little tap before every throw though, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball," Battle told reporters. "He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that gives the read the break. He's obviously dangerous with his feet.

"We know we got to be alert for that. Third and longs, they will run quarterback draws, and in the passing game, he will extend plays. So we got to be good downfield. DBs are plastering, so we got to be alert for that. He will take chances. We just got to be on, be alert on guys where they line up."

Bengals coaches surely can't be thrilled Battle revealed this information publicly before the game and gave Willis some time to adjust the tell prior to taking the field. After all, it would be anything but surprising if he fixes said tell by the time Sunday's game arrives, which means it won't be helpful to Battle and the rest of the defense.

It also isn't a stretch to wonder if the tell is one reason Willis has struggled this season.

He completed 56.3 percent of his passes for 712 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions in the first four games, which were all losses for the Dolphins.

The last game was the ugliest for the offense, as Miami managed just 10 points with Willis throwing for 85 yards in a loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

Perhaps now that it has been publicly revealed he has a tell, he can make the necessary adjustments and attack a Bengals defense that is an ugly 26th in the league in passing yards allowed per game this season.

articles.title: Chargers' McDaniel Talks Job Security amid 0-4 Start, Says Hot Seat Buzz 'Comes with the Territory'
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers are off to a disastrous start, and Mike McDaniel's offense has been the main reason for the team being 0-4.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers are off to a disastrous start, and Mike McDaniel's offense has been the main reason for the team being 0-4.

Naturally, his struggles have led to fans calling for his firing, but he understands that it's part of the job.

"When you have high expectations and you're getting the results we're getting and you're 0-4, that's pretty standard operating procedure," he told reporters Thursday. "I would be foolish, or I would feel entitled, if I didn't expect there to be disappointment."

Fixing Each Winless NFL Team Ahead of Week 5 👨‍⚕️

"And so, if you want things to change and you want narratives to change, you have to change them through action collectively. If our results are better, that's the only thing that matters. So it's pretty easy for me to focus on what I need to focus on."

The Chargers came into the season as a candidate to reach the Super Bowl, but now, they'd be lucky to reach the playoffs.

McDaniel, who took over as offensive coordinator this offseason after being fired by the Miami Dolphins, has an offense that ranks 28th in points per game (16.8).

Quarterback Justin Herbert ranks 21st in passing yards (816) and is tied for 22nd in passing touchdowns (4). His six interceptions are tied for the second-most among quarterbacks through four games.

McDaniel crafted some of the best offenses in recent memory in Miami, but he hasn't had the same success in Los Angeles thus far. Things won't get any easier this week as the Chargers face the Denver Broncos.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes left speechless by Brittany Mahomes’ witty Instagram move after Chiefs’ stunning victory
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes had plenty to celebrate after the Kansas City Chiefs erased a halftime deficit against the Las Vegas Raiders.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes had plenty to celebrate after the Kansas City Chiefs erased a halftime deficit against the Las Vegas Raiders. But one of the night’s most entertaining moments came away from the field. After Raiders coach Klint Kubiak confidently backed his team at halftime, Brittany Mahomes brought the comment back into the spotlight following Kansas City’s 30-27 comeback win. articles.title: New Cowboys Rumors on Joey Porter Jr.'s Illness with CB Surprisingly Out vs. Bucs
articles.summary: After making his debut with the Dallas Cowboys last week, Joey Porter Jr. won't be on the field on Thursday.
articles.body:
After making his debut with the Dallas Cowboys last week, Joey Porter Jr. won't be on the field on Thursday.

The cornerback was seemingly set to play against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, but was listed as inactive about an hour before kickoff. He is reportedly dealing with an illness that has caused him to vomit.

Porter played 25 snaps in his Cowboys debut against the Houston Texans last week and was hoping to get more action in his first game at AT&T Stadium, but he'll instead have to wait until next week to get back on the field.

According to NFL Network's Jane Slater, Porter was sick when he arrived at the facility and was sent home.

With Porter ruled out at the last minute, the Cowboys will likely turn to second-year corner Shavon Revel in his spot. Revel has been dealing with knee and ankle issues since Week 3 but is active for Thursday's contest.

The former third-round pick has logged nine tackles and a pass defended through his first four games this year.

The Cowboys acquired Porter from the Pittsburgh Steelers last week in return for a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick. Porter and the Steelers had previously struggled to reach a new contract before the season.

"We hope that this is not only an improvement in, just generally, our personnel, but we hope it really can be one that he really finds his level," Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said about the trade. "I would hope it would mirror maybe the George Pickens move that brought him in. I know that's a pretty high bar, that's pretty high expectations, but you have to have 'em to make a trade like this."

Porter had not yet played this season before being traded to Dallas, and he's now facing another setback. Whether his illness will carry into next week remains to be seen.

articles.title: Bengals' Jordan Battle warns Dolphins QB Malik Willis that he's been tipping passes ahead of Sunday's matchup

articles.body:
On the list of things not to say as an NFL player before a game, this is one of them.

The Cincinnati Bengals are set to visit the Miami Dolphins on Sunday as they seek to improve their 2-2 record. They apparently discovered an information advantage regarding Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis, whom they believe tips when he's about to pass.

Let Bengals safety Jordan Battle explain:

"He has a little slight little tap before every throw though, so I feel like we could use that as a key to break on the ball," Battle told reporters at his locker Thursday. "He likes to tap the ball before he throws it, or he takes his hand off, and that gives the read the break."

That's useful information that, if accurate, gives the Bengals a leg up on defending passes and creating turnover opportunities.

But now, thanks to Battle, the Dolphins are surely clued in on what the Bengals believe is Willis' tell. And if it's true, they'll have something to work on in Friday's practice ahead of Sunday's game. This appears to be a notable misstep from Battle.

That is, unless, Battle and the Bengals are up to some serious subterfuge, and they want the Dolphins to think that this is what they think. As in, I know that you know that I know what's going on, therefore the advantage is mine.

What if the Dolphins realize that tactic and respond accordingly? And so on and so forth. This is what's known in poker as a leveling war, which can lead to some extreme plays and exciting outcomes. Or for fans of "The Princess Bride," this .

But are Battle and the Bengals playing poker here? Or did Battle just give away part of the game plan?

articles.title: Brandon Staley Calls Out Troy Aikman After 'Not True' Comments About Saints DC During MNF Loss
articles.summary: New Orleans Saints' defensive coordinator Brandon Staley didn't appreciate ESPN analyst Troy Aikman saying that he didn't "have any answers" on defense and "knew it," given the team's injuries on that side of the ball, during Monday's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
New Orleans Saints' defensive coordinator Brandon Staley didn't appreciate ESPN analyst Troy Aikman saying that he didn't "have any answers" on defense and "knew it," given the team's injuries on that side of the ball, during Monday's 45-24 loss to the Atlanta Falcons.

Staley told reporters he had "no idea" what Aikman was talking about and refuted the comments "because they're not true."

"It was a tough night for us, and certainly, I'm responsible. I'm calling the defense, but we've got a great group of guys," Staley added. "No one defended that runner [Bijan Robinson] last year better than us. He's a hell of a player. But our group defended him twice last year better than anyone through his time in the NFL."

In two games last season, the Saints indeed held Robinson to 103 rushing yards and five receptions for 47 yards, keeping him out of the end zone. They did not have that level of success on Monday night, however.

The Saints gave up 420 yards of total offense in the loss and 145 rushing yards and two touchdowns alone to the electric Robinson.

That led Aikman to the commentary that irked Staley.

"Staley, he just simply doesn't have any answers. And I think he knew it when we talked to him coming in," the former NFL quarterback and longtime color commentator said during the broadcast. "I think he knew. He didn't tell us, but the guys that are out... their big edge-rushers and guys who can play the run and set the edge, they're not on the field, and they just don't have that star defender that can erase mistakes for other people. This was a matchup issue coming into this game, and it's proven true."

The Saints were missing players like edge-rushers Carl Granderson and Anfernee Jennings and linebacker Kaden Elliss, while Pete Werner was playing through a stinger.

Despite being short-handed Staley felt the game changed for the Saints on Atlanta's final drive of the first quarter, when a defensive holding penalty on fourth down gave the Falcons new life and Robinson scored one play later. The Falcons then scored on five of their next seven drives (and the two they didn't score on came at the end of each half).

"There were plenty of good moments in there in the first half, but after that possession, it was really up and down," he told reporters. "We did not play a good game after that fourth-down penalty. We never got our rhythm back as a defense. And that's what stood out to me. And that's why I say it was very uncharacteristic of us because, since I've been here, we've been very steady. But that game got away from us."

articles.title: D'Andre Swift Responds to Fumble Problems After Benching, Bears HC Calls Out 'Egregious' Error
articles.summary: D'Andre Swift has had a strong start to the 2026 campaign, but the Chicago Bears running back has struggled to keep the ball in his hands.
articles.body:
D'Andre Swift has had a strong start to the 2026 campaign, but the Chicago Bears running back has struggled to keep the ball in his hands.

After fumbling twice in the first four games, Swift believes it won't be a persistent issue throughout the season.

"That ain't me," Swift told reporters Thursday.

His most recent fumble came in Sunday's win over the New York Jets when linebacker Jamien Sherwood brought him to the ground and the ball popped out of his left arm. Bears head coach Ben Johnson didn't sugarcoat how he felt about the mistake.

"I think the one last week was egregious," Johnson said. "It's one that we can't have. There's too many times when the ball's getting away from our body and he knows that."

Swift didn't come back into the game after the fumble, with Kyle Monangai taking over as he picked up 146 yards and a pair of scores. Though he took accountability for the fumble, Swift didn't think being taken out of the game was a benching by Johnson.

"I wasn't really told anything, but I do understand that can't happen," Swift said. "So I take whatever comes with that. You know what I mean? I can't put the ball on the ground. I'm putting the team and everybody else [down]. I can't do that. I know that."

Monangai and Swift have been one of the best running back duos in the NFL this season, with Monangai rushing for 324 yards and three touchdowns and Swift adding 311 yards and three touchdowns.

Swift will look to continue his fast start to the year, while avoiding fumbles, against the Green Bay Packers on Sunday.

articles.title: Denzel Boston named early favorite for Offensive Rookie of the Year
articles.summary: Through four games of his first year, Denzel Boston has established himself as an early favorite for Offensive Rookie of the Year.
articles.body:
Through the first four games of his NFL career, former Washington Huskies wide receiver Denzel Boston has been one of the league's best rookies.

The second-round pick by the Cleveland Browns in April's draft has pulled in 13 catches for 284 yards (a number that leads all rookies and ranks No. 11 in the NFL), good for 21.8 yards per reception, and a pair of touchdowns while working with quarterback Deshaun Watson, as the team has gotten off to a 3-1 start thanks in large part to Boston's production.

On the NFL Stock Exchange podcast, draft analyst Connor Rogers named the 6-foot-4 wide receiver as the early favorite for Offensive Rookie of the Year.

"Denzel Boston is playing a role of an alpha wide receiver in terms of what they're asking of him, the usage, the plays he can make," Rogers said. "I think some of the plays that haven't ended up in the box score have been impressive as well."

"What's impressive when you watch him: his size allows him to draw targets down the field. He has that build-up speed, and you trust him to play above the rim, but he can go over the middle and break a tackle, and create a big play. We know he can impact the game as a blocker; it feels like he's quickly, quickly transitioning into that role as, 'I'm the guy' in this offense, especially when you're a perimeter threat like him."

Boston will have his next opportunity to assert himself as one of the NFL's top rookies on Sunday against the New York Jets, who have one of the league's best pass defenses, as it ranks No. 6, allowing just 193.3 yards per game.

articles.title: Warriors nearly took another prospect over Yaxel Lendeborg.
articles.summary: Yaxel Lendeborg had competition at the top of the Golden State Warriors big board on draft night
articles.body:
Yaxel Lendeborg has given the Golden State Warriors' fans a reason to be excited for the upcoming season. The rookie has impressed in his first two preseason outings, appears to be gelling well with his new teammates, and fills a needed role for the franchise. Factor in Lendeborg's NBA-ready skill set and his overall upside, and there's every reason to believe the Warriors have landed a stud with the 11th pick in the 2026 NBA Draft.

However, according to ESPN's Anthony Slater, Lendeborg wasn't the only name on Golden State's big board heading into draft night. Brayden Burries also had multiple fans throughout the organization and could have easily landed in the Bay Area had he been available when the Warriors were on the clock.

"On their final draft board in June, the Warriors -- who owned the No. 11 pick -- had Lendeborg and Arizona guard Brayden Burries ranked neck-and-neck, behind the consensus group of prospects up top," Slater wrote. "If Burries was there, team sources have indicated they would've drafted the 20-year-old combo guard for his upside. He had fans all over the organization."

The Milwaukee Bucks ultimately selected Burries with the 10th overall pick, taking him off the board just one spot too soon for the Warriors. Nevertheless, Lendeborg is already proving to be a strong fit for Golden State, so it's unlikely that there are any regrets over how things played out.

Lendeborg has started both preseason games he's played in and projects to be part of Golden State's starting five this season.

"He's going to play a ton," Kerr told ESPN. "Frankly, he deserves it. He's one of our best players already."

Kerr has already noted that the rookie is "unbelievably coachable," too. Burries may have been high on the Warriors' big board, but judging by how well Lendeborg fits, they landed the right guy for what the team needed.

articles.title: ‘He Keeps It Glued Together’ — Colin Cowherd Credits Cowboys QB Dak Prescott for Overcoming Chaos Surrounding Him in Dallas

articles.body:
The Dallas Cowboys are preparing for their upcoming Week 5 contest. It hasn't been the smoothest start to the season for Dak Prescott and his teammates, as Dallas is 2-2, though they are coming off a win over the Houston Texans.

The Cowboys expect to contend for a playoff spot once the season reaches the home stretch. Dallas has a ton of talent on the roster, and if things go according to plan, there is certainly a chance this team can contend.

However, one NFL analyst believes the Cowboys' chances of contention rest on the success of one man. Without Prescott under center, he believes Dallas could be in rather rough shape.

Colin Cowherd Lavishes High Praise on Cowboys' Dak Prescott

Colin Cowherd, during a segment on "The Herd w/ Colin Cowherd," discussed the Cowboys and where they stand at this point in the season. Without Prescott, he believes the picture wouldn't look so pretty.

"If the Cowboys are the world's biggest rock band, he is the manager. As they're trashing the hotel rooms, he's making the beds," Cowherd said about Prescott. "He makes sure he keeps it glued together; he gets everybody on stage as close to on time as you possibly can with the Dallas Cowboys."

Cowherd mentioned all sorts of things that Prescott has managed throughout his career. The veteran quarterback is talented on the field. But it's his presence on this team that could be one of his greatest strengths.

"If he's your kid, you make him the executor of the will. A stabilizing force. He's dealt with Dez Bryant and Ezekiel Elliott's immaturity early, Jerry (Jones') vanity always, now it's George Pickens' moodiness," Cowherd added. "Even in his rookie year… Tony Romo noticed immediately, to Romo's credit, the maturity."

Prescott has certainly been a leader for this team for a number of years. The Cowboys have been a playoff contender for much of his career to this point, as they have made the playoffs five times during Prescott's first 10 NFL seasons.

So far this season, Prescott has continued his strong level of play. Though Dallas has stumbled a couple of times, the quarterback play has been steady. He has thrown for eight touchdowns and just one interception this year.

Heading into Week 5, Prescott is ranked fourth on PFN's QB Impact Metric , with an impact score of 82.3.

Unfortunately, as previously mentioned, the Cowboys have faltered a bit this year. They began the season with a brutal loss to the New York Giants in Week 1. It was a frustrating 28-20 loss on Sunday Night Football and a difficult way to begin the new campaign.

Dallas did rebound in Week 2, picking up a win over the Washington Commanders. However, a trip to São Paulo, Brazil, brought another loss. The Baltimore Ravens defeated the Cowboys, and Dallas' coaches' questionable decisions cost the team.

As mentioned, Dallas is coming off a win in their last contest. They faced their intrastate rival, the Texans, and took care of business. It was a close game, but Prescott's 335 yards passing helped seal a victory.

Dallas has a short week this week. The Cowboys are playing on Thursday Night Football to kick off Week 5. Short weeks are never fun, but this is another opportunity for Prescott's leadership and maturity to guide Dallas once again.

articles.title: LIVE chat: Dallas Cowboys vs. Tampa Bay Buccaneers, ‘TNF’ Week 5
articles.summary: The Dallas Cowboys face the Tampa Bay Buccaneers under lights of Thursday Night Football in Week 5
articles.body:
It's already Week 5 of the 2026 NFL season, and yet again we have another NFC battle in primetime. Tonight, the 2-2 Dallas Cowboys take on the 0-4 Tampa Bay Buccaneers inside of Jerry's World.

Admittedly, this isn't an extremely exciting matchup on paper. First of all, it sure feels like NFC teams are getting a large percentage of primetime exposure to start the season. Second, the Buccaneers are dreadful right now, and the Cowboys are their typical selves. Dallas can light the scoreboard up with the best of them, and quarterback Dak Prescott is playing well right now, but their middling 21st-century ways continues with a .500 record.

Will Tampa Bay finally pick up a win, and on the road, or will Dallas get itself above .500 in Week 5? It's not going to be easy for the Bucs, which former Bills quarterback Ryan Fitzpatrick mentioned last Thursday in previewing this matchup.

Tonight, rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels gets the start with Baker Mayfield still recovering from a gruesome hyper-extended thumb on his throwing hand. It's already proven tough enough for Tampa Bay with Mayfield this season, so asking an undrafted rookie quarterback to make magic happen seems unwise. Daniels becomes the first undrafted rookie quarterback to start a game in Week 4 or earlier since the AFL/NFL merger in 1970.

Without a doubt, it's been an awful start for the Buccaneers. Being shorthanded as they are, it might prove difficult to take advantage of a putrid Dallas defense in primetime. No NFL teams has ever made the playoffs after starting 0-5, so you have to expect Tampa Bay to approach Week 5 like an elimination game.

With that, here's your open thread for Thursday Night Football . As always, be kind to one another — and in all things… Go Bills!

articles.title: What Broncos’ Sean Payton said about taking play-calling duties from Davis Webb
articles.summary: The Davis Webb play-calling era is over, or at least suspended, after just four games. Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton watched another Super Bowl appea...
articles.body:
The Davis Webb play-calling era is over, or at least suspended, after just four games. Denver Broncos head coach Sean Payton watched another Super Bowl appearance slip through his fingers last season when Bo Nix suffered a fractured ankle in the playoffs and a blizzard covered Empower Field during the AFC title game. He does not want to miss out on another opportunity to compete for a championship, and following a 2-2 start to the season, this intense individual is taking it upon himself to revitalize the squad's lackluster offense .

Following speculation that a more collaborative process would take effect , Payton clarified that he is replacing offensive coordinator Davis Webb as the Broncos' play-caller for the time being. He praised the former quarterbacks coach and pass game coordinator, declaring him a future head coach , per The Athletic's Nick Kosmider. "It's all ahead of him," the Super Bowl 44 champion said.

Webb has already garnered attention in the HC carousel and would have been a scorching-hot name if he succeeded in his new role with Denver this season. His ascension now hits a snag and puts his future candidacy in some uncertainty. Payton felt it was time for a change, though.

Is Sean Payton the magical elixir for this Broncos' offense?

The Broncos rank near the bottom or in the bottom half in most offensive metrics through the early portion of the campaign, averaging 18.5 points (27th), 81.3 rushing yards (29th) and 199.0 passing yards per game (20th). This squad's strength lies in its defense, but with Bo Nix entering his third NFL season, and the dynamic Jaylen Waddle joining the wide receiver room, a more dynamic offense was expected.

When a team makes a significant change to its game-planning process, players are bound to have strong reactions. Apparently, there is one specific emotion that is permeating the Denver locker room .

"{Everyone} is a little disappointed because you feel like you let your teammate down," Sean Payton said when asked about Nix's response to the Davis Webb news, per The Denver Post's Troy Renck.

No. 10 is less than six months removed from undergoing a second procedure on his ankle, so there is a chance that the offense improves as he becomes more comfortable moving around the pocket. Payton is not taking any chances, however. He has experienced great success in this role before and is banking on his expertise in 2026.

A week 5 meeting against a Los Angeles Chargers team (0-4) that is facing their own play-calling questions will be an important test for the Super Bowl hopeful Broncos. Opening kickoff will commence on Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET in SoFI Stadium.

articles.title: 49ers DE Romello Height inspired by Patrick Willis to play through broken hand
articles.summary: San Francisco 49ers rookie defensive end Romello Height said of playing with a bulky cast on his right hand after breaking it in Week 2: "At the end of the d...
articles.body:
It's hard to draw many similarities between Romello Height and Patrick Willis. In fact, it'd be foolish to do so. One guy is a rookie defensive end who has played in three NFL games; the other is arguably the greatest linebacker in San Francisco 49ers history.

There is one eerie similarity, however, even if it is born out of pure coincidence: Both players broke their right hands during a game while playing for the 49ers. Both players returned to said game, sporting bulky hard-shelled clubs while in significant pain. And both players went on to miss their first-ever NFL games, each against the Arizona Cardinals, due to the injury.

Height broke his hand early on in the 49ers' Week 2 win over the Miami Dolphins. He headed to the locker room and reemerged after halftime with his right hand wrapped in a white cast. In the second half, Height recorded his first NFL sack when he chased Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis out of bounds behind the line of scrimmage.

"I was going off adrenaline," Height said of his second-half performance in the 49ers' 35-13 win. "I felt pain, but it didn't matter at that point. I wanted to play for my brothers, and I wanted to finish the deal."

After further evaluation postgame, doctors determined Height's hand would require surgery. He had a procedure Sept. 22 that kept him out of the 49ers' subsequent contest against the Cardinals, before making his return in Week 4 against the Denver Broncos, starting and playing 37 snaps.

Every time Height dug his right hand into the grass at Levi's Stadium, or wrapped a player up for a tackle, or put a pass-rush move on an offensive lineman, he did so with a swollen right hand that had a large incision just above his index finger.

Protecting his hand was a club - a club so hard that when Height gave fellow rookie Jaden Dugger a fist bump, he questioned how Height was even playing. Beneath his club was "a lot" of protective padding, Height said, giving the cast so much bulk that it could only be compared to a boxing glove.

In 2010, Willis played just three days after undergoing surgery on a broken hand that he suffered during a December game against the Seahawks. After playing with that cast for multiple weeks, Willis underwent a second surgery ahead of Week 17 due to complications, which caused him to miss his first-ever NFL game. That snapped a 63-game streak to start his career. Willis also played with a cast on his hand for parts of his junior season at Ole Miss and in 2010 with the 49ers.

Height said he took inspiration from Willis' mentality.

"I just thought of it as: 'Something's just there,'" Height said. "It didn't stop my effort. It didn't stop me wanting to hunt the quarterback."

On the first play of the Broncos game, Height, seemingly out of the play after Jaylen Waddle had been tackled just beyond the line of scrimmage, sprinted over to the receiver and did a Superman leap over his body. Was it to test out his new piece of equipment? To see if he could still brace his fall with essentially one working hand?

"That was just me blacked out," Height said, "trying to get to the ball."

Height doesn't know how long he'll need to wear the cast during games. He doesn't care either, saying: "I mean, it's not really a difference for me. At the end of the day, I gotta go out and do my job."

"I love the way he competes, the way he plays," defensive coordinator Raheem Morris said. "He's gonna go out there regardless. He might have two clubs on and go out there. He's that kind of guy."

Thursday's practice: Nickel back Upton Stout (shoulder) returned to practice, wearing a blue non-contact jersey, after not participating on Wednesday. Head coach Kyle Shanahan had previously said the 49ers are hopeful Stout can play against Seattle.

Wide receiver Mike Evans (ribs) went from a limited participant Wednesday to a non-participant Thursday. Evans worked on a side field during the open viewing portion, as did defensive end Nick Bosa (calf) for the first time since suffering his injury ahead of a Week 3 practice. Shanahan said Thursday on KNBR that Bosa is "getting better each week," and that he is not "far from playing."

"We would love to get him out there before our bye week," Shanahan said of Bosa, "but still too early to tell."

Players who were upgraded to full participation on Thursday: running back Kaelon Black (illness), linebacker Dre Greenlaw (rest), running back Christian McCaffrey (rest) and tackle Trent Williams (rest).

articles.title: New Marvin Harrison Jr. Trade Rumors Reveal Colts as Potential Landing Spot amid Latest NFL Buzz
articles.summary: The Indianapolis Colts have interest in trading for Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., per ESPN's Josh Weinfuss and Stephen Holder.
articles.body:
The Indianapolis Colts have interest in trading for Arizona Cardinals wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., per ESPN's Josh Weinfuss and Stephen Holder .

"Sources told ESPN that the Cardinals are not shopping Harrison but other teams are still doing their due diligence on the third-year receiver. Those include the Colts, with a source telling ESPN that they would entertain the idea of trading for Harrison, the son of Marvin Harrison Sr., the Hall of Famer who owns multiple Indianapolis receiving records . "

ESPN's Adam Schefter previously reported on the Colts' interest during an appearance on the Pat McAfee Show .

Harrison, the No. 4 overall pick in the 2024 NFL draft, was considered one of the best wideout prospects in recent memory when he left Ohio State. He was a two-time All-American and finished fourth in the 2023 Heisman Trophy race.

Harrison showed promise in his rookie season, amassing 62 catches for 885 yards and eight touchdowns. However, he suffered two heel injuries, appendicitis and a concussion in 2025 and missed five games. His numbers dipped in that injury-impacted year (41/608/4).

This year has not gone well for Harrison. He has just five catches, 85 yards and one touchdown on 12 targets through four games. To put his usage in perspective, Harrison is fifth on the team in targets and has just one more target than backup running back Tyler Allgeier.

A change of scenery might be best for the Cardinals and Harrison. He isn't being featured in the offense (in fairness, he hasn't performed well lately), and he probably has a better chance of finding another team that can bring out the potential he showed in Ohio State.

The Colts have reportedly thrown their hat in the ring publicly and privately. Harrison would return to the city where his father, Marvin Harrison Jr., starred for the Colts and went on to become a Pro Football Hall of Fame wide receiver.

Alec Pierce is on injured reserve after suffering a re-aggravated left heel injury. He can return as soon as Oct. 25 against the Minnesota Vikings, but his timeline to get back to the field is unclear.

Keenan Allen is dealing with a groin injury that forced him to miss last Sunday (30-13 win vs. the Washington Commanders in London) and has him limited in practice this week. Ashton Dulin is out of practice this week with a groin injury.

Harrison could provide an immediate reinforcement for a position room hit hard by injuries. One can surmise he'd be a bigger focal point of the offense than he is in Arizona.

For now, Harrison remains a Cardinal, and he'll be on the field when Arizona hosts the Detroit Lions on Sunday afternoon.

articles.summary: Travis Kelce used his platform as a Kansas City Chiefs star to encourage fans to help families in need during the holiday season.
articles.body: Travis Kelce used his platform as a Kansas City Chiefs star to encourage fans to help families in need during the holiday season. His mother, Donna Kelce, also stepped forward for a charitable cause in Kansas City, joining Tammy Reid, the wife of Chiefs head coach Andy Reid, for the launch of the Light the World Giving Machines in November 2023.The initiative gave people a simple way to donate essential items to local and global charities. Rather than buying something for themselves, visitors could use the red vending machines to help someone else enjoy a better Christmas. How Donna Kelce and Tammy Reid helped launch Kansas City’s holiday charity driveOn Nov. 21, 2023, Donna Kelce and Tammy Reid took part in the unveiling of the Giving Machines at Union Station in Kansas City, Missouri. The machines returned to the city for the third consecutive year, offering residents another way to support families and individuals who needed help during the holidays.Donna, who is also the mother of former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce, had stayed in Kansas City after watching her sons face each other in the Chiefs-Eagles game on November 20. Her appearance at Union Station gave the NFL community another reason to connect her name with charitable work.The event brought together the Chiefs community and a wider effort organised through the Light the World campaign, which The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints facilitated. The Kansas City machines supported seven local charities and two global organisations.The local beneficiaries included Foster Adopt Connect, Kansas City Hospice & Palliative Care, reStart, Ronald McDonald House Charities of Kansas City, the Mayor’s Christmas Tree Fund, Science City and Westside Community Action Network.The choices covered different needs across the community. Visitors could donate meals, winter clothing, medical equipment and other essential items. The available options ranged from $3 to $150, allowing people to choose a gift that suited their budget. What Travis Kelce said about making Christmas better for familiesWhile Donna Kelce and Tammy Reid took part in the Kansas City launch, Travis Kelce helped spread the word through a promotional video shared by the Giving Machines Kansas City Instagram account in November 2023.“Check out the Giving Machine. It’s a big red box. You cannot miss it. Make sure you take the family down there and make a donation. Make someone else’s Christmas or holidays that much better. And, as always, go Chiefs, baby,” Travis said in the video.His message encouraged families to visit the machines and contribute to the campaign. It also showed how the Chiefs’ reach extended beyond football, with players and their families helping bring attention to a local charitable effort.The machines worked like cash-free vending machines. Visitors swiped a payment card, selected an item and paid for it on behalf of someone in need. According to KSHB's report, all donations went towards gifts specific to the participating charities.Kansas City was one of 61 cities across seven countries that hosted Giving Machines during the 2023 holiday season. articles.title: Tony Romo got disqualified from his Korn Ferry qualifier the same day he 'parted ways' with CBS Sports
articles.summary: Tony Romo was disqualified from a Korn Ferry Tour pre-qualifier for signing an incorrect scorecard on the same day he parted ways with CBS Sports.
articles.body: Man, it has not been a great run recently for former Dallas Cowboys star quarterback Tony Romo. Romo became the talk of the internet when he was arrested over the summer for operating a vehicle while intoxicated in Wisconsin. Police body cam footage of the arrest went viral, and his mugshot was quickly passed around, with a seemingly endless run of memes made about the 46-year-old. As one of CBS Sports' lead football analysts, speculation immediately started about his future on television, with the network announcing that he'd been put on indefinite leave. SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER That leave turned into a permanent separation in early October, when news broke that the two sides had agreed to mutually part ways. Obviously, not the best news for Romo, who, while he started off hot, had recently come under criticism from fans for his analysis and was still owed tens of millions of dollars on his contract. Well, the news got even worse for him that same day. Romo is an accomplished, very talented golfer, to the point where he recently participated in a pre-qualifier tournament for a Korn Ferry Tour event. Far from the PGA Tour, or more likely the Champions Tour, but still impressive for an "amateur" player. Less impressive? The fact that on the same day he "parted ways" with CBS, Romo was disqualified from that Korn Ferry pre-qualifier. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE While trying, unsuccessfully, to make the cut, Romo was accused of signing an incorrect scorecard. Per Golf.com, Romo's qualifier was held at the Club at Forest Ridge in Broken Arrow, Okla., where he started with rounds of 76 and 75, putting him well back, 13 strokes to be exact, of the leaders after 36 holes. That score was still good enough to put him in a decent spot to move on to the next stage of Q-School for the Korn Ferry tour. Put in a solid showing on Friday? He'd have given himself a realistic chance to advance. The problem? Three people had three different versions of Romo's score in that third round. Romo signed his score card showing that he made a 4 on the 16th hole and a 4 on the 17th hole. But his playing partner and marker, Brandon Rice, put him down for a 4 on the 16th, but a 5 on the 17th. That's odd, but even more bizarre is that a PGA Pro and walking referee told tournament organizers that after being assigned to track Romo's group after they were put "on the clock" for slow play, he recollected Romo having a 5 on the 16th and a 5 on the 17th. What on earth? THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Well, Rob Keller, the pre-qualifier administrator, told Golf.com what he thought happened. Keller believed that the slow-play, inability to make birdies, and "all that was going on with him," Romo simply didn't take the time to thoroughly check his marker's version of his score. Keller also added that Romo "took responsibility" when the two spoke on the phone while being "very complimentary" as to the quality of the tournament. Romo wouldn’t have made it through given his third-round score, but still, what a day for the former QB. How do you get your scores wrong? Especially when you know you have a marker there observing all of it. Sounds like Romo might be the ideal scramble tournament partner, one where the winning score is in the 40's somehow. articles.title: How did Jason Kelce go from criticising NFL referees to defending them? His stance shifted after two controversial incidents
articles.summary: Jason Kelce had plenty to say about the NFL’s decision to suspend two officials after separate on-field incidents involving Trey McBride and Eric Wilson.
articles.body: Jason Kelce had plenty to say about the NFL’s decision to suspend two officials after separate on-field incidents involving Trey McBride and Eric Wilson. The retired Philadelphia Eagles center initially criticised referee Adrian Hill for his treatment of Wilson during the Minnesota Vikings’ game against the Miami Dolphins. However, Kelce later changed his position during an episode of New Heights, the podcast he hosts with his brother, Travis Kelce.The debate grew after the NFL suspended Hill for one game and line judge Jeff Seeman for two games on Oct. 5, 2026. Both officials faced discipline for what the league described as unprofessional conduct toward a player. Kelce’s change of stance added another twist to a controversy that has raised questions about how the NFL should hold officials accountable when tempers flare during games. Jason Kelce initially backed Eric Wilson after his clash with Adrian HillDuring the Vikings-Dolphins game in Week 4, Miami running back Ollie Gordon II knocked Minnesota linebacker Eric Wilson into Hill, sending the referee to the ground. Hill got back up and shouted at Wilson, who appeared to be trying to help him stand.Kelce criticised the official’s response during New Heights, arguing that Wilson had not deliberately knocked Hill down. He said, “I have a bigger problem with this one. 'Cause clearly Eric Wilson did not try to do this. And then he’s trying to help him up, and then he gets mad at him. I think this is bogus.”His initial reaction focused on the circumstances behind the collision. Wilson had not appeared to intentionally bring Hill down, yet the exchange escalated after the official got back to his feet. The incident became one of two high-profile officiating controversies that prompted the NFL to review its officials’ conduct.However, Kelce did not stick with that position for long. Later in the same podcast discussion, he reconsidered his response and announced that he was retracting his criticism.“You know what? I’m retracting all this! I’m on the sides of both of these officials! I take the officials’ side!” Kelce said on New Heights””.His reversal gave the discussion a new direction, especially as the NFL faced criticism over the punishments handed to Hill and Seeman.Trey McBride incident and NFL referee suspensions spark a wider debateThe other controversy involved Seeman and Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. During Arizona’s 36-24 loss to the New York Giants, Seeman appeared to direct profanity at McBride after a third-down incompletion. McBride had disputed the lack of a pass-interference penalty against Giants cornerback Dru Phillips.Video of the exchange circulated online before the NFL announced Seeman’s two-game suspension on October 5. Hill received a one-game suspension for his interaction with Wilson.The NFL Referees Association challenged the severity of the penalties. On Tuesday, October 6, executive director Scott Green acknowledged that the officials’ conduct fell short of professional standards but argued that referees regularly face heated exchanges and verbal abuse from players and coaches.The NFL Players Association took a firmer stance on Seeman’s conduct. Executive director JC Tretter said officials should face the same standards as players when they cross the line.The league has disciplined players for their treatment of officials, too. In October 2025, Denver Broncos linebacker Dre Greenlaw received a one-game suspension without pay after chasing referee Brad Allen and verbally threatening him following Denver’s 33-32 win over the New York Giants. His appeal failed.Kelce’s change of heart did not settle the argument. Instead, it highlighted the difficult balance between protecting officials and holding them accountable. articles.title: Matthew Stafford’s message to Josh Allen reveals how seriously the Rams QB is taking the Bills superstar challenge
articles.summary: Matthew Stafford has a message for Josh Allen before Monday Night Football, and it comes with respect rather than trash talk.
articles.body: Matthew Stafford has a message for Josh Allen before Monday Night Football, and it comes with respect rather than trash talk. The Rams quarterback and reigning league MVP says Allen's presence gives the Bills real confidence and that few passers in the NFL are as talented. Two Super Bowl contenders meet Monday night, and the last time they did, in December 2024, the Rams won 44-42. Allen threw three touchdowns and ran for three more in that loss. He arrives this time after two shaky weeks that included four turnovers.How seriously is Matthew Stafford taking the Josh Allen challenge?Seriously enough to lead with praise. Stafford spoke to reporters this week and started with what Allen does for Buffalo. The tone was friendly, but the message was clear. Allen is the player the Rams have to solve."I got a ton of respect for Josh, what he brings to their team," Stafford said, via the team's official website. "Not only from just making the plays, but I just think his presence out there gives them a ton of confidence, as it should."Then he turned to his own defense, which has the tougher job on paper. "Obviously, I'm going against their defense, but understanding full well that our defense is facing a guy that is as talented as anybody in the NFL at the quarterback position," Stafford said. "So it'll be a big-time challenge for us as a team, as a unit. But we're looking forward to it."The respect makes sense. Allen came into the season as a favorite to unseat Stafford as MVP, but the last two games have not gone his way. He has four turnovers over that stretch, including a late interception that sealed last week's loss to the Patriots. A quarterback coming off that stretch has every reason to want a big night.What does Matthew Stafford say about Josh Allen's running and throwing?Stafford was never known for his legs, and at 38 he is not getting faster. That makes quarterbacks who can do both jobs a bit of a marvel to him."I'm in awe of a lot of those guys," Stafford said. "It's really cool to watch them do what they get to do, get out of some of the plays that they get out of, and make some of the plays with their legs."He then got specific about the red zone, where Allen does much of his damage. "Obviously, he does a great job of, (in the) red zone running the football, whether it's the sneaks on the 1- or 2-yard line, or even just making plays from the 5 or 10 getting in. So he's a lot of their offense, especially down there, but he's a one-of-a-kind player at the quarterback position."Monday's game also shows how long Stafford has been at this. articles.summary: The Tampa Bay Buccaneers survived a late comeback attempt by the Dallas Cowboys, sealing a 24-16 victory Thursday night with a game-clinching interception.
articles.body:
The Tampa Bay Buccaneers survived a late comeback attempt by the Dallas Cowboys, sealing a 24-16 victory Thursday night with a game-clinching interception.

Dallas entered the matchup as 8.5-point favorites over the Buccaneers at home, according to FanDuel Sportsbook . Tampa Bay entered Thursday's game without its starting quarterback but took advantage of a disastrous third quarter by the Cowboys to build a lead and hold on for the win.

Mayfield remained sidelined with a right thumb injury suffered in the Buccaneers' Week 3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

Rookie Jalon Daniels, a Kansas product, led Tampa Bay to its first win of the season in his second start.

After one quarter, each team had held possession just once, with the Cowboys scoring on a Javonte Williams run up the middle to cap a 4:09 drive.

The Buccaneers' first drive lasted 10:58, stretching into the second quarter, but ended with a 5-yard touchdown pass from Daniels to Bucky Irving to even the score at seven apiece.

A series of punts, six combined, and one more field goal by the Cowboys sent the teams into halftime, with Dallas leading 10-7.

It took Tampa Bay just one minute this time to find the end zone, with Irving setting the team up on a 72-yard run and Emeka Egbuka finishing the near-perfect drive with a 14-yard rushing touchdown to open the half.

Meanwhile, Dallas' disastrous third quarter was just beginning. Prescott threw an interception after six plays, with Buccaneers linebacker Yaya Diaby grabbing the ball.

Tampa Bay scored on its next possession, with Irving recording his second touchdown of the night as the Buccaneers took a 21-10 lead.

With 7:31 remaining and hopes of turning things around at home, KaVontae Turpin fumbled on the following punt return. The Buccaneers capitalized, getting into field goal position to extend their lead to 24-10 before forcing the Cowboys to turn the ball over on downs ahead of the fourth quarter.

With a chance to put the game out of reach with a field goal and extend their lead to three scores, the Buccaneers opted to go for it on fourth-and-goal but failed to convert, giving the Cowboys the ball back trailing 24-10 with 8:32 remaining.

In a worst-case scenario for Tampa Bay, it took Prescott just 2:13 to charge 99-yards down the field and finish the drive connecting with George Pickens in the end zone, cutting the deficit to one score despite a failed two-point conversion.

A three-and-out gave the Cowboys another chance, but a pass intended for Jake Ferguson bounced off his hands and was intercepted by Alex Anzalone. The Buccaneers then picked up a first down to seal the win.

Tampa Bay will host the Pittsburgh Steelers next Sunday at 1 p.m. ET, while the Cowboys will hit the road to face the Green Bay Packers later that day for Sunday Night Football, with kickoff scheduled for 8:20 p.m. ET.

articles.title: 'Extraordinarily Disappointing,' Jerry Jones Reacts to Cowboys Loss to Jalon Daniels, Bucs on TNF
articles.summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones provided blunt and honest assessments on  Thursday evening to describe his team's 24-16 home loss to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who started undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels for the second straight week in place of injured QB1 Baker Mayfield.
articles.body:
Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones provided blunt and honest assessments on Thursday evening to describe his team's 24-16 home loss to the previously winless Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who started undrafted rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels for the second straight week in place of injured QB1 Baker Mayfield.

A calm and poised Daniels performed very well, completing 19-of-25 passes for 189 yards and one touchdown while adding 23 rushing yards against a Dallas defense that allowed an NFL-high 6.4 yards per play through the first four weeks. The Cowboys also allowed Tampa Bay to amass 241 rushing yards and two scores, including 165 yards and a TD to running back Bucky Irving.

Despite the team's defensive performance, the Cowboys still had a shot to tie the game in the final minutes and had a 2nd-and-1 from the Tampa Bay 24-yard line with 1:22 remaining.

However, Dallas quarterback Dak Prescott's pass deflected off tight end Jake Ferguson and ended up in diving Bucs linebacker Alex Anzalone's possession for an interception.

Understandably, Jones was not happy watching Dallas' final drive end.

This has been a disappointing season for the 2-3 Cowboys, especially on defense.

They opened the season with a 28-20 road loss to the New York Giants, who possessed the ball for nearly 37 minutes and outgained Dallas 394-244.

Dallas rebounded with a 37-20 home win over the Washington Commanders. However, the Cowboys then lost a back-and-forth 34-31 thriller in Brazil to the Baltimore Ravens.

Dallas had a 1st-and-goal from the Baltimore two-yard line, down 31-28 with 23 seconds left, but lost in regulation after being held to a field goal and then allowing a 56-yard field goal by Ravens kicker Tyler Loop with no time remaining.

The Cowboys needed to overcome a 23-13 third-quarter deficit to win 34-30 against the winless Houston Texans last Sunday.

On paper, they looked like the clear favorites against Tampa Bay. Both sides of the ball struggled, though. Tampa Bay possessed the ball for 39 minutes and 21 seconds. The Bucs outgained Dallas 419-366. The Cowboys committed three turnovers, while Tampa Bay committed none. Tampa Bay also committed twice as many penalties (14 to seven) and still won by eight on the road with a backup, largely untested QB (albeit one who clearly showed his talent tonight).

The saving graces for the Cowboys right now are (a) the offense is good enough for the team to at least remain competitive, (b) Brandon Aubrey is still one of the best kickers in football, (c) the NFC East might be up for grabs this year given the Philadelphia Eagles' rough start and (d) six of Dallas' next seven opponents are at .500 or worse right now.

However, the defense continues to struggle despite an influx of talent still from last offseason, and it's unclear how it can be fixed through five weeks.

The trade acquisition of ex-Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who was out Thursday with an illness , should help, but the problems here go deeper than one player.

Dallas needs to figure something out, though, and hope no one else in the NFC East (perhaps the 3-1 Giants, who have the head-to-head tiebreaker on the Cowboys) runs away with the division before it's too late.

After four weeks of play, the NFL doesn't look anything like the league many expected entering the 2026 campaign.

The Cleveland Browns, Las Vegas Raiders, New York Giants and Minnesota Vikings own a combined 13-3 record. Conversely, the Houston Texans and Los Angeles Chargers have yet to win a game. The Super Bowl-bound Los Angeles Rams, based on preseason expectations, haven't been a dominant squad.

The Tampa Bay Buccaneers expected to compete for their fifth NFC South title in six seasons, especially after signing quarterback Baker Mayfield to a contract extension before the season began. Mayfield may be hurt, but the Bucs found a way to win their first game of the season during Thursday Night Football .

Bleacher Report NFL analysts Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton will follow all of the action and then break down each contest, provide takeaways and ask the most pressing questions.

RB Bucky Irving Drives Tampa Bay Buccaneers' Offense

With Baker Mayfield out of the lineup, undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels wouldn't be able to carry the Buccaneers' offense. He didn't need to when he could hand the ball to Bucky Irving.

Irving led the way Thursday with 165 yards on 21 carries, including a 72-yard run during the first play of the second half, which turned the game in an instant. He added two scores.

When Tampa needed a play late to milk the clock and secure the victory, Irving sealed the deal with a 22-yard run. Thursday's career-high effort happened at the exact right time for the Bucs to finally get into the win column after an 0-4 start. Can Jalon Daniels Usurp QB1 From Baker Mayfield?

The short answer is simple: No, Daniels is not going to become the Buccaneers' starting quarterback. But the undrafted free agent deserves credit for stepping into a difficult situation and playing well enough for Tampa to claim its first victory. Daniels still isn't driving the ball down the field, which will be necessary against better opponents. Plus, the Cowboys defense is counted among the league's worst, which can make anyone look somewhat better, especially when DaRon Bland drops what would have likely been a pick-six. Still, the first-year signal-caller used his legs to extend plays, completed most of his early throws and continued to get more comfortable in the pocket as the game progressed. At the very least, he showed why he was deserving of being the Bucs' QB2 this season.

Dallas Cowboys Defense Remains Dismal Last week's effort from the Cowboys' defense turned out to be an aberration. To be fair, Dallas allowed nearly 400 yards of offense against the Houston Texans. However, the unit played much better during key downs and slowed the Texans' run game. Four days later, Tampa Bay pushed past the 400-yard mark and did so with an undrafted rookie making his first NFL road start. The Cowboys' angles and tackling were abysmal. Dallas couldn't get a stop when absolutely necessary late in the contest. Clearly, the group is poorly coached, because the unit has too much individual talent to not improve eventually. Instead, the Cowboys rank 31st in total defense going into this weekend's action only because the Detroit Lions are the only team in the NFL surrendering over 300 passing yards per game. WR CeeDee Lamb Goes from Unstoppable to Injured Lamb obliterated the Texans defense this past weekend. After 17 receptions, Tampa Bay needed to key on him at all times, of course. Lamb finished Thursday's contest with two receptions for nine yards. Two things happened along the way. First, Lamb's presence allowed others to shine. Specifically, George Pickens posted season-highs with nine catches for 130 yards. Second, the five-time Pro Bowl receiver suffered a quad injury. Lamb tried to play through it during the second half, but he clearly wasn't comfortable. The loss coupled with Lamb's situation make the 2-3 Cowboys for more difficult to buy into as the season progresses.

articles.title: Brian Schottenheimer now sits on hottest seat in NFL after Cowboys collapse against Buccaneers
articles.summary: Bucky Irving's 72-yard run sparked a Tampa Bay Buccaneers comeback as rookie Jalon Daniels led the charge to upset the Dallas Cowboys at home.
articles.body: It’s official: Dallas Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer has the hottest seat in the NFL. Schottenheimer was stumped on the sideline at AT&T Stadium on Thursday night as his squad fell 24-16 to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, who entered the game 0-4 and started a rookie quarterback in his first career road game. Jalon Daniels was quite efficient against a reeling Cowboys defense, which came into this game as the third-worst in the league in terms of yards allowed per game (389.5) and fifth-worst in points allowed (28). The defensive side of the ball was a problem during Schottenheimer’s inaugural season leading the Cowboys in 2025, and with 34-year-old Christian Parker as defensive coordinator, it’s more of the same in 2026. Buccaneers head coach Todd Bowles is fighting for his job security after a brutal start to the season. Yes, his starting quarterback, Baker Mayfield, is out, but the Buccaneers did not look good before his injury. And since Tampa Bay couldn’t make the playoffs last season despite a red-hot start, Bowles needs to start stacking wins. The state of Tampa Bay, and a Dallas victory over the Houston Texans in Week 4, led Vegas to mark the Cowboys as a clear-cut favorite at home. But Dak Prescott never felt comfortable like he did in Week 4, with Bowles drawing up his signature blitzes throughout the four quarters, and the Dallas defense continued to be passive. Tampa Bay found itself down at halftime, 10-7, but shifty running back Bucky Irving changed the entire momentum of the contest when he sprinted 72 yards on the opening drive of the third quarter to set up an Emeka Egbuka touchdown. In just two plays, the Bucs went 86 yards and took the lead, shocking the sold-out crowd. To make matters worse, the Cowboys would turn the ball over their next three possessions, leading to a lopsided game. Prescott threw an interception, and Daniels found Tez Johnson in busted coverage for a 64-yard catch-and-run. Irving scored his second touchdown of the game to further the Bucs’ lead, and Prescott wouldn’t even get the ball back after KaVontae Turpin fumbled the ensuing kickoff, which Tampa Bay recovered. With a Chase McLaughlin field goal making it 24-10, the Cowboys felt desperate at the end of the third quarter, going for it on fourth down near midfield and failing to convert. There was, however, some hope provided by a key stop from this lackluster defense. On fourth-and-goal from the one-yard line, Bowles decided to go for the kill shot, hoping to punch one into the end zone and make it a 31-10 game in the fourth quarter. But Sean Tucker, their short-yardage specialist in the backfield, was unable to punch it home. From there, Schottenheimer put on his best play-calling hat and recognized that momentum was shifting toward Dallas despite the Buccaneers’ 99-yard drive. He and Prescott delivered. George Pickens capped that 99-yard drive with a 17-yard touchdown catch, his first of the season, to make it a one score game after a two-point conversion failed. The momentum continued, as the Buccaneers went three-and-out, and with ample time as well as timeouts, Prescott could go down the field and perhaps tie the game with a touchdown and two-point conversion. Instead, more disaster for the Cowboys in this primetime matchup, as tight end Jake Ferguson, usually as sure-handed as they come for Dallas, had a Prescott pass go right through his hands, hit his face mask and land in the arms of Buccaneers linebacker Alex Anzalone while in Tampa Bay territory. This time, Daniels and the Buccaneers’ offense didn’t squander the chance to put the Cowboys away, as Irving picked up the necessary first down to allow his rookie quarterback some victory kneels to end the game. But Jerry Jones demands winning in Dallas, and this was a brutal loss for a coach already stirring speculation about whether he’s right for one of the most coveted jobs in the sport. There’s still many games left to play, but it’s truly heating up for Schottenheimer after this one.

articles.title: Matt Goncalves carries his late father's dream every time he takes the field
articles.summary: Colts guard Matt Goncalves, who spent his first two seasons dealing with new work, is becoming one of the NFL’s best offensive linemen
articles.body:
INDIANAPOLIS — Matt Goncalves has always understood the power of belief.

His father, William, always believed deeply in his son's ability to play professionally.

From the time he was little until his father passed away following a battle with cancer last October, Goncalves could lean on his father's confidence, a belief that helped carry him from Eastport-South Manor High to Pittsburgh to the Colts , all the way to a starting job in his second season in the NFL.

"He made me love the game, he made me believe in myself," Goncalves said. "An important thing is, it helped me believe in myself as much as my dad did. He believed in me more than everybody."

Indianapolis Colts vs Washington Commanders photos in NFL Week 4 action

The talent was there. When the Colts drafted Goncalves in the third round of the 2024 draft, they thought they were taking a future right tackle.

Goncalves made nine starts at tackle as a rookie, building confidence in his ability to play at the NFL level, then got shifted to fill a hole on the interior of the offensive line. He'd been a tackle for most of his life; playing guard required Goncalves to essentially spend his first season as a starter in rookie mode, learning on the fly while starting for the Colts.

But that first season as a starting guard clarified what he needed to do in the offseason.

"The strength aspect of it," Goncalves said. "Working different body positions, being in a three-point stance, how to fire out off of that. Striking quickly, because they're on top of you before you know it. Understanding that, maybe a different scheme, it definitely brings a different perspective into what you want to incorporate in your training."

Goncalves also realized he needed to get his mind in a different place.

He had spent his first two seasons learning, and there's an inherent uncertainty that comes with trying to pick up something on the fly.

"This is the NFL," Goncalves said. "It's hard. It's a lot of stress, it's a lot of anxiety. You have expectations to perform, it's kind of hard to get to that state to kind of believe in yourself and be confident. You're worrying about this, that and the other thing. When you kind of just block those things out, focus on your job, have fun, believe in yourself and know the play, it'll take care of itself."

Goncalves needed to develop the kind of belief that his father always had in him.

"I made a lot of changes in my attitude and my mindset," Goncalves said. "Just go have fun. Believe in myself; I think belief is a powerful thing."

When he returned to the Colts this offseason, Goncalves was a different kind of player.

Even if he didn't realize it at first. A reporter asked Goncalves in training camp if he felt like a veteran, and at the time, he wasn't sure how to answer. Goncalves isn't the type of player to sing his own praises.

Four games into the season, Goncalves can see a difference now.

He knows the position, knows how he's supposed to approach positional drills to fix his technique or take it to the next level. When he gets into the building every morning, Goncalves knows everybody he's passing in the hallways, knows the routine he has to use to get ready for Sunday.

"That gives me confidence," Goncalves said. "'I've got this, I'm a vet.'"

The rest of the Colts offensive line can tell a difference.

"He's poised, he's a pro," left tackle Bernhard Raimann said. "He takes care of all the little details. You can see how much he prepares every week, how much winning matters to him."

The Indianapolis offense is off to a rough start, and young Colts right tackle Jalen Travis is going through growing pains.

But the right guard has been a rock for Indianapolis, stabilizing the right side of the line next to Travis. Goncalves has not given up a "blown block" in the passing game, according to Sports Info Solutions, and he's been almost perfect in the run game as well, a rarity for a lineman after four games.

"His technique, the way he finishes blocks, his physicality in the run game, his poise in pass pro, his hands, it's been great," Raimann said. "It's been phenomenal."

Goncalves has also become the kind of lineman that young players like Jalen Farmer can watch and try to emulate.

"Works really hard at it," Colts quarterback Daniel Jones said. "No surprise, he's playing at a high level."

Every time Goncalves puts his hand in the dirt, he thinks of his dad, who died almost a year ago.

When he plays on Pittsburgh's field again this weekend, those thoughts will likely be even stronger, given his history in college.

"This is our dream together, to get to this level," Goncalves said. "I have two other brothers. Obviously, they played basketball, baseball. His dream was to see his sons go play for a professional sports team."

He's gotten to the point his father always believed he'd reach.

articles.title: Derrick Henry has no doubts over who the NFL’s best running back is right now
articles.summary: Derrick Henry has named Bijan Robinson as the NFL’s best running back ahead of the Baltimore Ravens’ Week 5 clash with the Atlanta Falcons. The Ravens star w...
articles.body:
Derrick Henry has named Bijan Robinson as the NFL's best running back ahead of the Baltimore Ravens' Week 5 clash with the Atlanta Falcons.

The Ravens star was asked about Robinson ahead of Sunday's matchup and had no hesitation in giving the Falcons running back the top spot.

Robinson enters the game with 494 rushing yards, the second-most in the NFL, despite a slow start to the 2026 season. His form has taken off since Michael Penix Jr. returned in Week 3.

Derrick Henry backs Bijan Robinson ahead of Ravens-Falcons clash

Robinson has rushed for 339 yards and four touchdowns across Atlanta's last two games, helping the Falcons secure wins over the Green Bay Packers and New Orleans Saints.

Henry, meanwhile, has 374 rushing yards this season and ranks fourth in the league. That sets up a fascinating battle between two of the NFL's leading backs when the teams meet in Atlanta.

Henry was quick to praise Robinson when asked about his performances, saying: "He's the best in the game right now, he's doing it all. I ain't gonna shy away from it. He's doing a great job, hell of a back.

"He does a great job in their system. Then [he] does a great job when the play is not exactly how they want it, he knows how to make guys miss, and be able to get vertical, and get the most out of a play, for sure."

Henry also admitted that while he does not know Robinson particularly well, the two have spoken on social media.

"I'm sure I'll talk to him after the game," Henry added.

Robinson will now have the chance to back up Henry's huge compliment on the field. The Falcons will face a Ravens defence that could use three-linebacker packages specifically designed to limit his impact.

Baltimore is also dealing with uncertainty at quarterback with Lamar Jackson nursing an ankle injury. Regardless of who starts under centre, Henry and Robinson are likely to be central to what could be one of Week 5's biggest individual battles.
